correctness.rationale: For a vertex cover S, two edge-distance vectors can agree only if the edges have the same selected endpoint set. A collision therefore reduces to two edges sx and sy with x,y outside S. The independent complement, the clique/path attachment geometry, p2, and a selected nonattachment clique vertex eliminate every such case. Thus every vertex cover edge-resolves. Minimum-size and counting formulas are then exact vertex-cover calculations. Direct exhaustive verification checked every vertex cover on 40 lollipops.

value.rationale: Lollipops are a standard family combining a clique and path through the simplest bridge attachment. The theorem identifies a structural collapse of dominant edge metric dimension to ordinary vertex cover on the entire family, proves every cover works, and classifies and counts every minimum basis. This is a natural infinite-family fact about the interaction of two constraints, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
